horizon_driver: European Commission 5-year mandate (current college seated Dec 2024) overlaid on national electoral cycles (France legislative crisis-driven, Germany 4yr); effective horizon shortened by recurring national budget/no-confidence cycles, notably France's

constraints.source: German/Dutch/Nordic 'frugal' bloc opposition; NGEU (2020) was framed as one-off, capped at EUR750bn to end-2026
constraints.breaks_under: systemic bond-market stress (e.g. simultaneous French/Italian spread blowout) forcing an NGEU-style emergency repeat

constraints.source: Treaty on European Union unanimity requirement for CFSP and own-resources decisions; single member (Hungary, Belgium) can and does block
constraints.breaks_under: coalition-of-the-willing workarounds already used for defense procurement (SAFE) and reparations-loan structuring outside full Council unanimity

constraints.source: Belgian/Euroclear legal-risk objections (litigation exposure, precedent for EU companies' assets in Russia); European Central Bank warnings about euro reserve-currency credibility
constraints.breaks_under: already partially breaking: Dec 2025 Council deal advanced a EUR90bn loan structure backed by the assets' income stream (not outright seizure) after overcoming Belgian and Hungarian objections
already broken via the national defense-spending escape clause activated for 18 member states as of Feb 2026, and via France's persistent ~5% deficit

stated_vs_revealed.stated: The EU is building 'strategic autonomy' and reducing security dependence on the United States.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Actual capability delivery remains slow and US-dependent: the EUR800bn Readiness 2030/ReArm Europe plan and EUR150bn SAFE borrowing instrument are still in early disbursement, and national procurement (Germany's EUR35bn military-space plan to 2030, France's EUR4.2bn 2026-2030) is incremental relative to the scale of the stated ambition.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Rhetorical urgency (post-2022) far outpaces fielded capability; genuine autonomy is a decade-scale project being sold as an urgent one.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: The EU is united and moving toward genuine fiscal solidarity ('more Europe') following the NGEU precedent.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: NGEU borrowing authority expires end-2026 with no agreed permanent successor; France's 2026 budget crisis (two governments fell over it, deficit still ~4.6-5.4% of GDP) was resolved through purely national political bargaining, not EU fiscal transfers. Meanwhile Italy's spread to Germany has compressed to ~100bps (better fiscal discipline than France), inverting the classic 'north-creditor/south-debtor' script the Cartographer anticipated.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The real fault line in 2026 is not a clean north-south split but France (a founding core state) becoming the fiscal outlier, while Italy converges toward German-level credibility.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: The EU stands unified in isolating Russia and mobilizing frozen assets for Ukraine.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Belgium blocked outright confiscation for over a year on legal-risk grounds (Euroclear litigation exposure, Moscow court already awarding Russia's central bank a $230bn damages claim against Euroclear); the Dec 2025 compromise used an income-backed loan structure specifically to avoid the precedent of outright seizure, and Belgium continues to demand joint liability guarantees ('golden goose') as of Sept 2026.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Unity exists on sanctions maintenance but not on the harder question of asset seizure, where a single small member state has effective veto power for over a year.

tripwires.if: France's 10-year OAT spread to Bund sustains above ~90-100bps for 2+ consecutive quarters with a further government collapse
tripwires.then: EU moves toward an ad hoc emergency support mechanism outside standard SGP process, replaying the NGEU pattern rather than genuine permanent fiscal union

tripwires.if: Belgium's guarantee demands remain unresolved beyond mid-2027 and the EUR90bn loan tranche stalls
tripwires.then: a coalition of the willing (likely UK+EU core minus Belgium/Hungary) structures a bilateral or G7-adjacent workaround that bypasses full EU unanimity, weakening the Commission's claim to sole custodianship of the Russia-asset question

tripwires.if: a Baltic/Black Sea sabotage or grey-zone incident directly implicates Russian state action against EU infrastructure
tripwires.then: escalate capability triggers rapidly (sanctions tightening, accelerated joint procurement) even without full unanimity, using existing escape-clause and SAFE-style precedents

what_would_change_my_mind: A sustained, multi-quarter widening of French spreads alongside a fifth failed government would be evidence for genuine fragmentation risk requiring a split into a French-led debtor cluster vs a German/Dutch/Nordic creditor cluster. Current evidence (Italy's spread convergence, defense-spending convergence across 18 states under the escape clause) argues against splitting the actor for now — recommend keeping ST_EU merged but tracking the France-specific fiscal fault line explicitly as a distinct sub-state risk rather than a north-south bloc division.
